title: Stochastic kernel probing and model acceptance runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures a pragmatic approach to introducing stochastic kernel probing and a tightened model acceptance + rollback checklist for speculative decoding integrations. It is intentionally operational: quick tests, probe schedules, metrics to watch, and an explicit rollback matrix.

Context and motivation:
- We want to experiment with multiple kernel execution paths at request time to find better throughput/latency tradeoffs for diverse token lengths and hardware combos.
- Probing should be safe: no KV cache corruption, bounded latency regressions, deterministic fallbacks, and clear telemetry so we can accept or rollback a model+kernel combo quickly.
- Existing docs cover speculative decode theory; this doc is the runbook engineers should use when doing an integration or canary that exercises stochastic probing at scale.

High-level probing model (operational):
- On canary traffic, select up to N_probe kernels per request according to lightweight sampling policy. Default N_probe=2.
- Probe policy: 10% of requests are flagged eligible; of these, 75% use existing (baseline) kernel + 25% attempt an alternate kernel candidate. This keeps perturbation small.
- Probe budget: limit probe attempts to 1 probe per request and a global probe QPS cap per model shard (configurable).
- Probe duration window: probes should only run during the canary epoch (see rollout plan) and only for the first M tokens of a conversation for stateful models (M default 32).

KV cache safety rules (non-negotiable):
- All probes MUST operate on read-only copies of KV cache or on snapshots. No in-place mutation.
- Snapshot semantics: copy-on-write shallow snapshots are acceptable provided reference lifetime ends before request completion.
- If snapshotting fails or memory pressure is detected, disable probing for that shard and emit a dedicated alert.
- After a successful probe path, KV coherence verification runs asynchronously: checksum comparison between baseline and candidate outputs for identical prefix sequences (sampled).
- If checksum mismatch rate > 0.5% on sampled checks within 1 minute, disable candidate kernel immediately and mark for investigation.

Acceptance criteria (for model+kernel variant):
- Latency SLO adherence: p99 latency increase relative to baseline <= 10% (absolute thresholds depend on model/class).
- Token-level throughput: median tokens/sec for matched requests >= baseline - 5%.
- Correctness signal (synthetic/real prompts): decoded-output divergence (BLEU/ROUGE or task-specific metric) <= regression tolerance (default 1.5%).
- Error budget: new errors (timeouts/exceptions) <= baseline + 0.1% in canary cohort.
- KV checksum mismatches <= 0.5% on sampled traffic in rolling window.
- Cost guardrail: estimated per-token GPU-seconds <= baseline * 1.12.
- Operational readiness: tracing enabled, debug logs for probe paths, and rollout toggles present in console.

Canary rollout plan (practical steps):
1) Dry run in staging: run distributed probe simulation on synthetic workload, exercise KV snapshotting, and assert no memory leaks after 1M tokens.
2) Smoke canary (internal): 0.1% of internal dev traffic, 1 hour. Validate telemetry.
3) Customer canary: 1% of eligible customer traffic for 6 hours. Monitor live telemetry and run offline correctness sampling.
4) Ramp: 5% for 12 hours, 20% for 24 hours, then full traffic if no regressions.
- At every step: check acceptance criteria; if any criterion violated beyond configured threshold, trigger rollback immediately.

Rollback matrix (quick reference):
- Severity: KV_CORRUPT (checksum mismatch > 0.5%) -> Immediate rollback + global disable of probing for that model. Postmortem priority: P0.
- Severity: LATENCY_P99_REGRESSION (p99 > 10% relative) -> Pause ramp and reduce probe fraction by 50% for 30 minutes; if persists, rollback. Postmortem P1.
- Severity: ERROR_SPIKE (>0.1% increase) -> Immediate rollback for canary cohort. P1.
- Severity: COST_OVERAGE (cost > 12% increase) -> Pause ramp; require economics sign-off to continue. P2.

Telemetry & dashboards (must-have signals):
- Kernel adoption rate by request class (short/medium/long sequences).
- Probe success/failure counts, with failure reasons (OOM, snapshot-fail, exception).
- KV checksum mismatch rate (sampled).
- Latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) segmented by kernel path.
- API error rates and exception types.
- Cost per million tokens and GPU-seconds per token.
- Sampling of decoded outputs for automated QA comparison jobs.

Synthetic test harness (recommended):
- Lightweight harness that replays representative prefix distributions and verifies: latency, token throughput, decoding parity for first N tokens, and KV snapshot memory delta.
- Include deterministic RNG seeds for decode determinism in synthetic tests.
- Run harness nightly on staging and after every PR that touches kernel selection or KV path.

Operational checklist (pre-canary):
- [ ] Tracing enabled and trace-ids surface probe path (so we can correlate latency to kernel decision).
- [ ] Probe toggle and global QPS cap implemented and accessible from console.
- [ ] Alerts wired for checksum mismatch, p99 jumps, and OOMs specific to probe workers.
- [ ] Memory and CPU profiles recorded for probe vs baseline paths.
- [ ] Owned rollback procedure documented in runbook and rehearsed in tabletop exercise.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is a safe default sample size for decoded-output parity checks across diverse tasks? (Need empirical study; propose 2000 per canary epoch).
- Should KV checksum be computed on the raw KV bytes or canonicalized representation? Raw bytes are fastest but brittle across kernel implementations.
- Explore adaptive probing where kernel candidates with consistent wins get higher sampling weight. Design scheduled for Q1.

Notes to self / experiment log snippets:
- 2024-11-10: initial probe harness found a transient 0.8% KV mismatch when alternate kernel changed packing layout. Switched to canonicalized KV view; mismatch dropped to 0.02%.
- 2024-11-22: small customers in eu-west saw latency p95 bump during probe due to CPU-side marshaling; reduced probe fraction and added async marshalling experiment.

Appendix: quick commands and toggles (ops shorthand)
- Enable probes for model X: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/admin/probes -d '{"model":"X","enabled":true,"fraction":0.01}'
- Force rollback: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/admin/probes/rollback -d '{"model":"X","reason":"KV_CORRUPT"}'
- Check probe metrics: open dashboard /dashboards/serving/probes?model=X

If you take nothing else away: keep probe perturbation small, default to snapshot-only KV access, and ensure a fast, unforgiving rollback path. This is an experiment surface — safe defaults > theoretical best-case.
